summary: Max is push-based. An event (a click, a MIDI note, a metro tick) hands a message to one object, and that object sends messages on down its cords until the chain ends. Only a hot inlet (usually the left) makes an object compute and output; cold inlets just store a value. Audio is separate: once DSP is on, the signal graph is computed one vector of samples at a time, whether or not anyone listens. Jitter GL drawing is driven by a render context that bangs its clients once per frame.
details: Every computation starts with an event; Max hands it to the high-priority scheduler or the low-priority queue, then handles it by sending a message to an object [scheduler.json]
Hot inlets trigger output; cold inlets change state without output, e.g. the right inlet of + [objects.json]
What an object does depends on the first atom of the message (the selector) and on which inlet receives it; most messages work in any inlet, e.g. 'frequency 440' to cycle~ [messages.json]
Signal objects run in blocks once DSP is on; there is no pull model that skips unused signal branches [patch_cords.json, preferences_and_settings.json]

Work is only skipped where you ask: poly~ voices can be muted via thispoly~, MC wrapper channels via @usebusymap, a subpatcher's signal objects via mute~ or pcontrol [polyphony.json, mc/mc_poly_without_polytilde.json, mute~.maxref.xml]

jit.world renders automatically when @enable is 1 (default 0), at @fps (default 30) or synced to the display; GL objects in the same patch are added to its context and video objects get automatic output [jit.world.maxref.xml]
Gen has no messages at all: everything inside gen~ runs synchronously every sample, so there are no hot/cold inlets [gen/_gen_overview.json]
strengths: The cause of every output is visible: something upstream fired. Cold inlets let you load values first and fire once.
costs: Nothing is lazy. Idle audio and unseen branches still cost CPU unless muted by hand. A value arriving at a cold inlet silently does nothing until the next hot message.
open_questions: Max's docs do not state outright that unused signal branches are computed; it follows from the absence of any pull mechanism and from the existence of mute~/busymap.

summary: Within one event, Max is depth-first: each path is followed to its end before the next path starts. Several cords from one outlet fire right to left by the position of their destinations. trigger makes order explicit and is the recommended tool; load order is staged but Max advises not to rely on it.
details: Messages traverse the patcher depth first: a path goes to its terminal node before adjacent paths get anything [scheduler.json]
Cords leaving one outlet are sorted right to left [illustration_mode.json]
trigger 'outputs any input received in order from right to left' [trigger.maxref.xml]
Max says not to assume load order; use trigger to make it explicit [patcher_lifecycle.json]
Several receive objects with one name receive in a non-deterministic order (repo, quoting the refpage) [patching/MAX_PATCHING.md]
Inlet and outlet order of a subpatcher or abstraction follows the left-to-right position of its inlet/outlet boxes; poly~ uses numbered in/out instead [abstractions.json, polyphony.json]
Message boxes with commas send several messages in sequence; defer reverses order by jumping to the front of the queue, deferlow keeps order [messages.json, scheduler.json]
In gen there is no firing order: all operators fire together [gen/_gen_overview.json]
Parameter-enabled objects initialise in their 'Order' attribute order, lower first [parameter_mode.json]
strengths: Order is deterministic and can be read from layout and trigger arguments. Illustration Mode and the debugger make it visible.
costs: Order depends on screen position, so moving a box can change behaviour silently. Fan-outs without trigger are a classic bug source.

summary: Max has a millisecond scheduler for timed (high-priority) events, the audio sample clock for DSP, a frame clock for GL rendering, and a tempo-based transport. Time values can be fixed (ms, hh:mm:ss, samples, hz) or tempo-relative (ticks, note values, bars.beats.units at 480 PPQ). Scheduler in Audio Interrupt ties scheduler time to the sample clock. The NonRealTime audio driver runs audio as fast as possible.
details: High-priority events (MIDI, metro, pipe, delay) carry a time; low-priority events are handled first-in first-out [scheduler.json]
With SIAI on, the scheduler is serviced once per signal vector and uses the audio sample counter, not wall time [scheduler.json]
With SIAI, sig~, click~, line~, curve~ and vst~ take scheduled events sample-accurately; snapshot~, peakamp~, edge~ etc. output them sample-accurately, one vector late [sample_accurate_messages.json]
Scheduler slop (default 25 ms) is how far the scheduler may fall behind real time before it corrects [scheduler.json]
One global transport (reserved name 'internal') plus any number of named transports; metro and timepoint use @transport to pick one; resolution is always 480 PPQ [transport.json]
Fixed units: ms, hh:mm:ss, samples, hz. Tempo-relative: ticks, 4n/8nt etc., bars.beats.units; positions vs intervals differ, and translate converts [time_value_syntax.json]
In Max for Live, unnamed transport objects follow Live's transport but cannot control it [transport.json, m4l/live_timing.json]
NonRealTime driver disables hardware I/O and runs DSP as fast as possible; jit.record @realtime 0 and jit.world @enable 0 + bang give frame-by-frame video [non_realtime.json]
jit.mo.time outputs time values in sync with jit.world for animation [packages/jit.mo/docs/jit.mo.time.maxref.xml]
strengths: Musical time is built in and shared by name. SIAI gives sample-accurate control events when needed.
costs: Several clocks coexist and the user must pick the right one for each job. Scheduler, audio and frame timing drift relative to each other unless deliberately linked.
open_questions: No documented global timeline or keyframe clock exists outside the transport. How GL frame time relates to transport time is not documented beyond jit.mo.

summary: Messages are made of atoms: bang, int, float, symbol, and lists of them. Larger data is never sent itself: a cord carries a name (jit_matrix u123, jit_gl_texture name, dict name, string, array) that points at storage. Signals, MC signals, matrices, GL textures and half-edge geometry each have their own cord style. Conversion is done by dedicated objects.
details: Atoms: bang, int, float, symbol; a list is ordered atoms; strictly a list starts with a number, otherwise the first symbol is a selector [message_types.json]
Int vs float matters; some objects behave differently or refuse one [message_types.json]
Named storage types: matrix (CPU), texture (GPU), dictionary, string, array — passed by name in a message [message_types.json]
Six cord kinds: event, signal, MC, Jitter matrix, GL texture, Jitter geometry [patch_cords.json]
Matrices have 1–32 dimensions, any number of planes, and type char, long, float32 or float64; image planes are ARGB [jitter/matrix.json, glossary_common_terms.json]
Gen works only in 64-bit floats; no int/float distinction [gen/_gen_overview.json]

Converters (registry): sig~, snapshot~, number~; jit.catch~, jit.release~, jit.peek~, jit.poke~, jit.buffer~; jit.gl.asyncread (texture to matrix, one frame late) [obj-qlookup.json, jitter/textures.json]
OSC arrives as an opaque FullPacket message that must not be stored [OSC.json]
typeroute~ splits a cord's messages by type [message_types.json]
strengths: Passing names instead of data makes big data cheap to route and lets many objects share one store. Cords show their type by colour.
costs: Symbols vs lists vs selectors and int vs float are subtle and cause silent misbehaviour. Data carries no metadata beyond its type; units and meaning live in the patcher's head.

summary: Max keeps control rate (events), audio rate (signal vectors) and frame rate (render loop) apart, with explicit converter objects between them. poly~ voices can up- or down-sample locally; pfft~ runs a spectral sub-rate. Many channels travel in one MC cord, and MC wrapper objects hold one copy of an MSP object per channel.
details: Signal vector size and I/O vector size are global audio settings [preferences_and_settings.json]
poly~ takes 'up N' and 'down N' arguments for local resampling [poly~.maxref.xml]
pfft~ loads a patch and handles windowing and overlap-add [frequency_domain.json]
gen~ runs per sample; gen runs at message rate; jit.gen/jit.pix per cell; jit.gl.pix per pixel on the GPU [gen/_gen_overview.json]

MC cords carry many channels; mc.xxx~ wraps N instances; @chans fixes the count, otherwise it adapts to the widest input; a changed @chans takes effect only after audio restarts [mc/mc_wrapper.json, mc/mc_messages_to_wrapper.json]
Several MC cords into one inlet sum, and the result has the widest cord's channel count [mc/mc_patchcords.json]
mcs.xxx~ is a single instance whose inputs and outputs are bundled into one MC inlet/outlet [mc/mc_mcvsmcs.json]
Up to 1024 logical audio channels map to physical hardware channels [audio_channels.json]
Fast event streams into low-priority objects (snapshot~ into v8) can back up the queue; speedlim, qlim, onebang reduce the rate [scheduler.json]
strengths: Each domain runs at its natural rate and the boundaries are explicit objects. MC makes N-channel and polyphonic work one cord wide.
costs: Crossing rates is manual and easy to get wrong (stepping, backlog, lost timing). MC channel topology (interleaved vs separate) has to be managed by hand.

summary: A .maxpat saves structure, not state: objects, cords, arguments and frozen attributes. Slider positions and number values are lost on reopen unless a storage system keeps them. Max offers several: Snapshots (embedded, all parameters), preset and pattrstorage (slots, interpolation, JSON files), per-object embed flags (dict, coll, table, v8 script text), and initial values on parameters. Loading runs in fixed phases.
details: Saving keeps names, connections, arguments and frozen attributes; the value of sliders and number boxes is not usually saved [pattr.json]
Inspector shows unsaved attributes in italics; the snowflake freezes one so it is saved [inspector.json]

Snapshots save every parameter-enabled object in a patcher hierarchy and are embedded in the patcher; plugin/amxd/rnbo snapshots live in the Max 9 Snapshots folder unless embedded; no interpolation; subpatchers cannot have their own [snapshots.json]
preset stores UI state in the patcher file; pattrstorage stores pattr clients, interpolates, and saves to a JSON file named after it, @savemode 0–3 [presets_and_interpolation.json, pattr.json]
dict @embed, coll @embed and table @embed (table default 1) save data in the patch; buffer~ and jit.matrix contents cannot be stored with pattr [dict/coll/table refpages, pattr.json]
v8 can save state with a save() function calling embedmessage, and join pattr via getvalueof/setvalueof [javascript.json]

Load phases: object creation, cords, parameter initial values, pattr @autorestore, loadbang/loadmess, live.thisdevice, window, patcherargs/loadmess deferred, dspstate~; subpatchers before parents in each phase [patcher_lifecycle.json]
Close order: closebang then freeing (freebang); subpatchers first [patcher_lifecycle.json]
Editing an object's text or encapsulating it creates new objects with reset state [objects.json, subpatchers.json]
strengths: Several storage systems fit different needs, and pattrstorage adds interpolation and a readable JSON file. Load order is staged and documented.
costs: The default is to lose state, so every patch needs a deliberate storage choice. Several overlapping systems (snapshots, preset, pattr, embed, initial values) make 'what will reopen?' hard to answer.

summary: Settings are attributes, set by name with a message or @name in the box. A smaller layer, Parameter Mode, turns an object's state into a named parameter with range, type, unit style, initial value and visibility. Parameters are what Snapshots, MIDI/key mapping, Live automation, OSC addresses and param_connect use. There are no expressions on attributes.
details: Attributes appear in any order after arguments as @name value; most have a setter message of the same name; attrui and getattr show and watch them [objects.json]

Parameter Mode adds Long Name (unique in the hierarchy), Short Name, Type (Int 0–255, Float, Enum, Blob), Range, Initial Enable/Value, Unit Style, Exponent, Steps, Order, Visibility [parameter_mode.json]
live.* objects always have parameters on; every parameter-enabled object must have a scripting name [parameter_mode.json, scripting_overview.json]
Mapping binds MIDI or computer keys to parameters per patcher, with min/max/exponent/steps, relative, trigger and pickup modes; not available in Max for Live [mapping.json]
Integrated OSC gives each parameter an address /<patcher>/param/<name>/<attr>; OSCQuery is optional; param.osc is the object form [OSC.json]
param_connect binds a UI object to a parameter inside gen, rnbo~, v8 (declareattribute), poly~ (param) or jit.gl.slab, both ways, without cords, same patcher only [param_connect.json]
Gen param and RNBO params appear as attributes of the box [param_connect.json]
In Max for Live, Parameter Visibility decides automation, storage in the Set and control-surface access [parameter_mode.json]
strengths: One parameter definition feeds presets, mapping, OSC, Live and UI links. Attributes make object state readable in the box.
costs: Parameter Mode is opt-in per object, so coverage is patchy. Attributes cannot hold expressions or bindings; any link between values is cords or param_connect.
open_questions: Whether integrated OSC covers all parameter attributes beyond raw and normalized values was not fully read.

summary: Three forms: an embedded subpatcher (p), an abstraction (a .maxpat used by name from the search path) and a bpatcher (a patcher shown as a UI block). Abstractions take arguments via #1–#9 or patcherargs and get a unique #0. poly~ and mc.poly~ replicate one patcher many times. Prototypes, snippets, templates and packages handle styling and sharing.
details: Subpatchers are embedded and independent copies; abstractions reference one file, so editing one edits all [subpatchers.json, abstractions.json]
Ports come from inlet/outlet boxes, ordered by position; @comment gives hover text [abstractions.json]
#1 replaces with the first box argument; patcherargs outputs arguments and @attributes at load; #0 is unique per instance, only at the start of a word [abstractions.json, glossary_common_terms.json]
Subpatchers cannot use arguments or #0 [subpatchers.json]
bpatcher can embed or reference a file; shows presentation if the inner patcher has openinpresentation; size from openrect [bpatchers.json]
poly~ loads one copy per voice (1–1023) and routes by note/midinote/target; mc.poly~ and mcs.poly~ give MC I/O [polyphony.json, poly~.maxref.xml]
Abstractions open read-only; a .maxhelp with the same name becomes the help file [abstractions.json, patching.json]
Packages bundle patchers, externals, help, docs, prototypes, snippets; package-info.json has a semantic version [packages.json]
Gen has its own abstractions (.gendsp/.genjit) [gen/_gen_overview.json]
strengths: Any saved patch is instantly a reusable object, with arguments and help. Replication (poly~, MC) is built in.
costs: Versioning is file-level only: no per-instance version pinning, and editing an abstraction affects every patch that uses it. Port order follows box position, so layout edits can rewire parents.
open_questions: No documented versioning of abstractions beyond package version strings.

summary: Most names are global to the whole Max application: send/receive, value, buffer~, dict, coll, named transports, and the targets of semicolon messages. Narrower scopes exist: pv (one patcher and its children), #0 (one abstraction instance), --- (one Max for Live device), scripting names (one patcher), pattr paths (one root hierarchy). GL objects find their context by name with @drawto.
details: receive names are global; any send or the REPL reaches every receive of that name [repl.json]
value shares across the app; pv only within a patcher and its subpatchers [value/pv refpages]
#0 makes a per-instance name inside an abstraction and its subpatchers [glossary_common_terms.json]
In Max for Live the name space is global across devices; --- at the start of a name makes it per device [m4l/live_symbols.json]
Scripting names (@varname) are unique within one patcher; thispatcher and v8 getnamed use them [scripting_overview.json]
pattr systems are per root patcher; pattrmarker gives a root a global name used as ::name [pattr.json]
Semicolon message boxes send to named global receivers like max and dsp [messages.json]
jit.gl objects bind to a context by name; without @drawto a texture binds to the first context found, undefined when there are several [jitter/graphics_processing.json, jitter/textures.json]
Gen send/receive are local to one gen patcher [gen/_gen_overview.json]
strengths: Wireless links are one word, and scope can be narrowed when needed. Names make large patches routable without cords.
costs: Global is the default, so two copies of a patch or device collide silently. Each container has a different scoping mechanism to remember.

summary: Max has no built-in scene, cue or timeline layer. A work is one patcher graph (often with subpatchers or tabs), and its structure is built from objects: qlist and coll for cue lists, pattrstorage or Snapshots for states, the transport for musical time. Parts are turned on and off with mute~, pcontrol, gate and similar objects.
details: qlist stores timed or untimed cues as messages sent out or to receive objects [qlist.maxref.xml]
mtr records and plays messages; seq and detonate play MIDI and scores [mtr/seq/detonate refpages]
pattrstorage slots and interpolation, preset with recallmulti and nodes, give state recall between sections [presets_and_interpolation.json]
mute~ disables a subpatcher's signal objects; pcontrol disables all its objects; pass~ outputs zero when muted [mute~/pcontrol/pass~ refpages]
Global transport and timepoint fire events at musical positions [transport.json, timepoint.maxref.xml]
Projects can open several top-level patchers and run Open Actions on load [projects.json]
strengths: Any show logic can be patched exactly as wanted.
costs: Every show rebuilds cueing and section switching from parts; there is no standard cue list or timeline to hand to an operator.
open_questions: No userguide topic covers show structure; this is assembled from refpages. No timeline object is documented in Max 9 (no timeline refpage found).

summary: Controls are UI objects placed in the patcher; each one is a node in the dataflow, so the value it shows is the message it sends. Presentation Mode gives a second, independent layout of chosen objects as the performer view. Parameters can also be mapped to MIDI, keys, OSC, Live, and Mira on an iPad. Custom UI can be drawn with v8ui/jsui or a jspainter file.
details: Lock to perform, unlock to edit; Operate While Unlocked allows both [patching.json]
Presentation shows only objects with @presentation, at their own presentation_rect; a patcher can open in presentation [patching.json]
Message box right inlet displays a message; print logs every message [messages.json]
attrui shows and sets any attribute of the object it is cabled to; Inspector rows can be dragged out as attrui [objects.json, inspector.json]
param_connect binds a UI object to a supplier parameter without cords and keeps both in sync [param_connect.json]
bpatcher embeds a patcher's interface as a block [bpatchers.json]
v8ui and jsui draw with MGraphics; @jspainterfile redraws an existing UI object [custom_ui_objects.json, javascript.json]
mira.frame mirrors a patcher region to connected iPads [packages/mira/docs/mira.frame.maxref.xml]
Styles, prototypes and color themes set appearance [prototypes.json, glossary_common_terms.json]
strengths: The interface and the program are the same graph, so controls cannot drift from data. Presentation gives a clean performer view without a separate build.
costs: UI is hand-placed; nothing is generated from parameters. Building and keeping two layouts (patching and presentation) is manual work.

summary: Max is live: the patch keeps running while you edit it, and new objects work the moment they are created. Changing an object's text replaces it with a fresh instance, losing its state. With audio on, an optional mixer crossfades between old and new versions of the DSP graph. The scheduler can be stopped to edit a busy patch.
details: Edits happen in unlocked (edit) mode while the patch runs [patching.json]
Changing an object's text usually creates a new instance and resets its state [objects.json]
Mixer Crossfade (adds latency) crossfades old and new DSP after edit operations [preferences_and_settings.json]
Edit > Stop Scheduler (Cmd-period) halts metro, pipe, delay and MIDI while you edit [scheduler.json]
Gen recompiles automatically in the background while you edit; auto-compile can be turned off [gen/_gen_overview.json]
v8 autowatch / node.script @watch relaunch code when the file changes [node.script.maxref.xml; repo CLAUDE.md for v8]
Pref 'Edit Operations Trigger Loadbang' decides whether pasted or undone loadbang/loadmess fire [preferences_and_settings.json]
Undo and Redo exist (mentioned in preferences) [preferences_and_settings.json]
strengths: No compile-run cycle; you hear and see every edit at once.
costs: Retyping an object loses its state, and some edits briefly glitch audio unless crossfade is on. There is no 'blind' edit mode that keeps changes off the live output.
open_questions: Max's docs do not describe undo depth or what undo restores. A blind or staged editing mode is not documented.

summary: JavaScript is built in: v8 and v8ui (and older js/jsui) define objects in JS, can query and change the patcher, and run on the low-priority thread. node.script runs full Node.js in a separate process. Lua runs inside jit.gl.lua, Java in mxj, GenExpr in gen codeboxes. The graph itself can be built and rewired by thispatcher messages or the JS patcher API, and the REPL sends text commands.
details: v8 handles messages by function name (bang, msg_int, list, anything), sets inlets/outlets, has loadbang, save, getvalueof; require loads CommonJS modules [javascript.json]
JS always runs at low priority; high-priority input is deferred to it; no setTimeout, use Task [javascript.json]
Scripting can create, delete and connect objects, open files, walk the hierarchy, using scripting names, thispatcher or JS getnamed [scripting_overview.json]
node.script: a local Node.js process controlled by 'script start/stop'; @watch and @autostart; Node v20.6.1 [node.script.maxref.xml, Node for Max/README.md]
jit.gl.lua embeds Lua with direct OpenGL calls [lua/jit_gl_lua_overview.json]
mxj runs Java classes as Max objects [mxj.maxref.xml]
GenExpr in gen codebox; v8.codebox and node.codebox are top-level code boxes [gen/_gen_overview.json, new_in_max9.json]
REPL: send messages to named receivers and ::scripting names, evaluate JS, 'man' for docs [repl.json]
Semicolon messages to max and dsp control the application [messages.json]
strengths: Many languages, and scripts behave like ordinary objects in the graph. The patch can program itself.
costs: JS runs at low priority, so it is unsuited to tight timing. Each language has its own API and threading rules to learn.

summary: Errors go to the Max Console as text, colour-coded and linked back to the object that posted them. Missing objects load as broken boxes and unknown attributes are mostly silent. The debugger adds watchpoints, breakpoints and stepping on cords; probes show the last message, signal or matrix on a cord; Illustration Mode runs the patch in slow motion.
details: Console colours: grey status, yellow warning, red error, blue internal error; double-click finds the object; filter by object or regex [max_console.json]
Common errors: No such object, doesn't understand, bad arguments, inlet out of range [error_messages.json]
print, error and console objects write or capture console text [max_console.json]
Watchpoints print, monitor or break; Step walks the call stack; debugging only works with Overdrive off [debugging_and_probing.json, scheduler.json]
Event, Signal and Matrix probes show cord contents on hover or in a window [debugging_and_probing.json]
Illustration Mode slows execution and queues new events per outlet [illustration_mode.json]
Stack overflow from a feedback loop disables outputs until cleared; DSP loops are refused [scheduler.json]
threadcheck reports which thread a message runs on [threadcheck.maxref.xml]
Audio CPU meter and FPS meter in the patcher window [patcher_window.json]
strengths: Strong cord-level tools: probe any cord, break on any cord, watch the order of events.
costs: Many mistakes produce no error (unknown attributes, cold-inlet values, wrong order). There is no per-object CPU profiler documented.
open_questions: Max's docs do not document a per-object or per-patch CPU profiler beyond the global audio CPU meter.

summary: Jitter GL uses named render contexts (jit.world, jit.pworld, jit.window + jit.gl.render) that objects join by @drawto. Draw order is decided by depth testing by default; @layer orders objects only when @depth_enable is 0 on those objects, and @blend_enable mixes them. jit.gl.node makes offscreen contexts, jit.gl.pass adds post passes, and materials attach via jit.gl.material or jit.gl.pbr. Matrices run on the CPU; textures, slab, pix and pass run on the GPU.
details: jit.world wraps jit.window, jit.gl.render, jit.gl.node, jit.gl.cornerpin and jit.phys.world [jit.world.maxref.xml]
Objects bind to a context by name; @drawto picks one when there are several [jitter/graphics_processing.json]

All scene objects share @layer, @depth_enable, @blend_enable, @blend; depth testing overrides layer, so disable it on objects to layer; layer 0 order is indeterminate; higher layers draw on top [jitter/depth_layer_blend.json]
jit.gl.layer is an alias of jit.gl.videoplane with depth_enable 0 and blend_enable 1 by default [obj-qlookup.json, transform-defaults.json]
@depth_write 0 + @layer lets a transparent object use the depth buffer without hiding what's behind [jitter/depth_layer_blend.json]
jit.gl.node with @capture 1 is an offscreen target; jit.world @output_texture captures the whole render [jitter/graphics_processing.json, jitter/textures.json]
jit.gl.pass loads .jxp pass files, needs a material on geometry, and works with jit.gl.node [jitter/render_passes.json]
Several jit.gl.camera objects can render to viewports of one context [jitter/graphics_processing.json]
Instancing: jit.gl.multiple (per-instance matrices) or jit.gl.buffer + jit.gl.tf (stays on GPU) [jitter/graphics_processing.json]
Engine is glcore (OpenGL core) by default since 8.5; gl2 is legacy [jitter/graphics_engine.json]
GL position units: ±2 spans the window (repo, forum-derived) [scans/c74-forum/forum_insights.md]
strengths: Contexts are found by name, so GL objects need no cords to draw. CPU and GPU paths both exist, with explicit conversion.
costs: Draw order is implicit (depth or layer 0 is indeterminate) unless the user sets layer and depth_enable on each object. Two pipelines (matrix and texture) must be kept apart deliberately.
open_questions: What depth_enable does when set on jit.gl.render itself is not described: the refpage lists the attribute without text, and jit.world's refpage does not list it.

summary: Max runs a main (low-priority) thread for UI, files and JS, an optional separate high-priority scheduler thread (Overdrive), and the audio thread. Audio can be split across threads per top-level patcher (mixer parallel processing) or across poly~ voices (@parallel). Jitter matrices run on the CPU; textures, shaders, gen jit.gl.pix and transform feedback run on the GPU. Gen compiles patches to machine code or GLSL. Cost is shown mainly by the audio CPU meter and the FPS meter.
details: Overdrive runs high-priority events in their own thread; recommended for MIDI/audio, off for Jitter; disables debugging [scheduler.json]
SIAI runs the scheduler inside the audio thread; expensive scheduler work then causes dropouts [scheduler.json]
Some objects always run at low priority (file loads, drawing, dialogs, v8) [scheduler.json, javascript.json]
Enable Mixer Parallel Processing processes each top-level patcher's audio in its own thread [preferences_and_settings.json]
poly~ @parallel spreads voices over processors; disabled when hosted by Live [poly~.maxref.xml]
Gen chains compile to one meta-object; gen~ optimises by update rate [gen/_gen_overview.json]
Texture-matrix copies are slow; jit.gl.asyncread avoids blocking at one frame of delay [jitter/textures.json]
Event backlog can crash Max; speedlim/qlim reduce rate [scheduler.json]
CPU Limit pref and 'dsp cpulimit' skip audio vectors over a threshold [preferences_and_settings.json, controlling_max_with_messages.json]
In Max for Live, Jitter runs in Live's interface thread, so frame rate depends on Live's UI and buffer size [m4l/_m4l_overview.json]
strengths: Clear priority lanes keep timing-critical work ahead of UI. Gen and GPU paths give compiled speed inside the patch.
costs: Thread behaviour depends on global settings, so the same patch can behave differently on two machines. Cost is not shown per object.
open_questions: Whether Jitter matrix objects use multiple CPU threads is not documented in the topics read.

summary: Max has no built-in multi-machine session. Networking is done with objects: udpsend/udpreceive and integrated OSC (with OSCQuery) for control, jit.net.send/recv for matrices over TCP, Syphon and Spout packages for sharing textures with other apps on one machine, Node for Max for anything web-based, Mira for iPads, and rnbo.remote for exported RNBO devices.
details: Integrated OSC exposes parameters by address via a built-in UDP server; OSCQuery serves over HTTP [OSC.json]
udpsend, udpreceive, osc.packet, osc.codebox in the registry [obj-qlookup.json]
jit.net.send sends matrices and messages over TCP to jit.net.recv [jit.net.send.maxref.xml]
Syphon and Spout are Package Manager packages used to send textures to apps like OBS [jitter/video.json]
node.script runs Node.js, giving access to npm networking [node.script.maxref.xml]
mira.frame mirrors patcher regions to iPads [mira.frame.maxref.xml]
rnbo.remote controls a remote RNBO device's parameters, MIDI, clock and presets [rnbo.remote.maxref.xml]
RNBO mentions Ableton Link support [rnbo.json]
strengths: Open protocols (OSC, UDP, TCP, Node) make Max easy to connect to anything.
costs: Clock sync, state sharing and failover across machines must be built by hand.
open_questions: No documented Max-level clock sync between machines (Link object or MIDI clock sync) was found in the core docs read; jit.gl.syphonserver is named in the userguide but its package is not installed here.

summary: A patch can ship as a project (.maxzip archive), a collective, or a standalone application that bundles the Max runtime. Max for Live devices (.amxd) are frozen bundles that run in Live. Plug-ins and Max for Live devices can be hosted in Max with vst~ and amxd~. RNBO exports patches to plug-ins, C++, JavaScript/Web Audio and Raspberry Pi; Gen exports C++ and GLSL.
details: Standalone = Max runtime + collective; built from a project or the Collective Editor; configured by a standalone object (@appicon_mac, @gensupport, @cefsupport) [standalones_and_collectives.json]
macOS standalones need signing/notarisation to avoid permission prompts [standalones_and_collectives.json]
Projects consolidate dependencies and archive to .maxzip; recommended for collaboration with Git [projects.json, standalones_and_collectives.json]
Devices are projects; freezing embeds dependencies, including externals for both platforms if found [projects.json, m4l/live_freezing.json]
A Max-for-Live-only licence cannot save Gen/MC/Geometry patches, export Gen code, build standalones or reach audio/MIDI drivers [m4l/live_limitations.json]
vst~ / mc.vst~ host AU, VST, VST3; amxd~ hosts devices [plugins.json]
RNBO (paid add-on) exports to VST/AU, Raspberry Pi, C++ and JS [rnbo.json]
Gen exports C or GLSL [gen/_gen_overview.json]
Project Open Actions can set ;max overdrive 1 etc. on load [projects.json]
strengths: Many targets, from a desktop app to a plug-in to embedded hardware via RNBO.
costs: A standalone is a whole Max runtime, not a lean player. Plug-in export goes through RNBO, a separate language and product.
open_questions: Unattended running (watchdog, auto-restart, kiosk) is not documented in the topics read.

summary: New objects can be written in C (Max SDK) or C++ (Min), in JavaScript (v8/v8ui, jspainter), in Java (mxj), in Lua (jit.gl.lua), as GLSL shaders (.jxs for jit.gl.slab), as gen patches (.gendsp/.genjit), or as plain abstractions. All appear as ordinary boxes; externals are found on the search path at launch, and packages bundle them with help and refpages.
details: Externals are .mxo (macOS) / .mxe64 (Windows) found on the search path at launch; they run with Max's permissions [externals.json]
Max SDK (C) and Min (C++) for externals [externals.json]
v8 objects can declare attributes (declareattribute) that param_connect sees [param_connect.json]
JXS files declare shader params that become object attributes [jitter/jxs_file_format.json]
jit.gl.pass .jxp files bind shader params to Max attributes with <bind> [jitter/render_passes.json]
Abstractions become objects by file name; .maxhelp of the same name is the help [abstractions.json]
Packages hold externals, javascript, patchers, docs (refpages), help, init, interfaces [packages.json]
ABL objects wrap Ableton Live devices and DSP components [abl.json]
strengths: Many ways to add parts, and every one looks like a normal object to the user.
costs: Externals are binary and platform-specific (architecture errors on Apple Silicon/Intel). Python is not a built-in option.

summary: Files are found by name through the search path: the patcher's folder, its project, the Max 9 folder, then user paths. Path prefixes (Patcher:, Project:, Package:, ~:) give relative paths. Projects track and consolidate dependencies; standalones and frozen devices bundle them. Some objects load files synchronously at creation and asynchronously later.
details: Search order: patch folder, project, Max 9 folder, search path folders [search_path.json]
Prefixes: ~:, C74:, Usermax:, Desktop:, Tempfolder:, Package:, Project:, Patcher: [search_path.json]
Projects show explicit and implicit dependencies, consolidate, de-consolidate and archive [projects.json]
Dependencies named in a message box are not detected automatically for collectives [standalones_and_collectives.json]
A file argument loads synchronously at object creation; later replace is asynchronous (buffer~) [patcher_lifecycle.json]
File loads always run at low priority [scheduler.json]
viddll engine: loadram pulls a whole movie into RAM; Default Cache Size pref for jit.movie/jit.playlist [jitter/video.json, preferences_and_settings.json]
Video engine avf (mac default) or viddll; HAP supported natively [jitter/video_engine.json]
File Browser and Collections organise search-path content; 'max paths' prints paths in use [file_browser.json, standalones_and_collectives.json]
strengths: Name-based lookup makes patches portable when files travel together. Projects automate collecting dependencies.
costs: Two files with one name on the path resolve by search order, silently. Missing media show up only as console errors.
open_questions: No documented relink tool for missing media was found; the only mentions are 'Search for Missing Files' in standalone settings.

why_system_level: Max contains whole languages with different evaluation rules (gen, RNBO, GLSL shaders) inside ordinary boxes. Where a patch's logic sits changes rate, ordering, types and exportability for everything inside.
summary: Max hosts compiled sub-languages inside boxes. gen~, gen, jit.gen, jit.pix and jit.gl.pix hold gen patchers: no messages, no UI, everything synchronous, all 64-bit floats, compiled to machine code or GLSL. rnbo~ holds a Max-like language made for export. The same box shape therefore hides very different rules.
details: In gen there are no messages; all operators fire at once; no hot/cold; in, out, param connect to Max [gen/_gen_overview.json]
Feedback in gen~ needs history (one-sample delay) or delay [gen/_gen_overview.json]
Gen operators are not Max objects and are absent from Max's object registry (repo finding) [CLAUDE.md, obj-qlookup.json]
RNBO objects are based on Max objects and are exportable; gen runs inside RNBO [rnbo.json]
param in gen/RNBO become attributes of the box and param_connect targets [param_connect.json]
strengths: Sample-level and pixel-level code without leaving the patcher, and code that can be exported.
costs: Names repeat across languages with different meanings, and the boundary is easy to forget.

why_system_level: It decides how a reader can trust what a patch shows, and it shapes saving, editing and documentation across every object.
summary: An object box shows its creation arguments and typed attributes, not its current state. Messages change the state without changing the box. Retyping the box makes a new object. Some arguments set structure (inlet counts) that can never change after creation.
details: Arguments initialise an object and do not reflect its current state, e.g. + 10 after a right-inlet message [objects.json]
Some arguments (gate's outlet count) cannot be updated after creation [objects.json]
Attributes can be set later by message, and frozen in the Inspector to save a value [objects.json, inspector.json]
Changing box text replaces the object and resets state [objects.json]
Defaults for attributes are listed per class in transform-defaults.json (708 classes, repo count) [transform-defaults.json, CLAUDE.md]
strengths: Box text is a compact, readable record of how each object starts.
costs: What you see is not what is running; state must be shown with displays or attrui.
